title: Canonical OpenNetwork and S1
fixed_parameters: Canonical Holant.OpenNetwork over Bool, CommSemiring R; boundary order and actual vertex/edge records retained. BoundaryComplement itself works over any finite D without Nonempty D.
runtime_inputs: Semantic network and boundary assignment, not a byte machine. All boundary assignments are quantified.
promises: Raw uses the actual boundary-image complement. Corrected tensor adds a hidden copy of the raw boundary and n explicitly oriented boundary-kernel occurrences. Corrected disjoint composition requires the original common EdgeKind W and per-edge hypotheses; raw composition permits mixed kinds.
outputs: S1 partition equals canonical raw or corrected tensor, separately. Actual canonical disjointUnion and boundary-reorder commuting laws; ordinary/closed compatibility with the prior S1 bridge.
resources: Instance-generated palette includes actual vertex functions and edge kernels; corrected palette explicitly includes boundary kernels. It does not grant those tables to an arbitrary fixed language.
cost: Noncomputable semantic conversions and equivalences; no codec, polynomial bit-time, fixed-language reduction, planarity or degree-preservation theorem.
nontrivial_examples: Paired disequality stub raw [3,2], tensor [2,3]; first composition 21/14, boundary swap 10/15, second composition 20/45. Empty-domain generic assignment cases explicitly covered.

title: Exact fixed-gadget elimination
fixed_parameters: Finite signature/edge layouts, arity function, fixed well-formed Template family. ExactField fixes FixedField K n and rational coordinate ExactSignatureTables; no runtime language/field search.
runtime_inputs: Original validated RawClosedNetwork encoding. Local gadget-realization identities are hypotheses; compiler correctness, output-size and machine costs are proved.
promises: Ordered graph records with loops, parallel edges, nullary vertices and empty graphs; each repeated macro occurrence receives fresh internal-edge blocks. Prefix extension requires explicit arity agreement and exact table-prefix/local-realization hypotheses.
outputs: Literal compiler output and exact value equality. Nat tables give F1 ParsimoniousReduction. ExactField uses the same coefficient-coordinate F.encoding on source/target and original PolyTimeOracleReduction with identity answer recovery.
resources: No implicit equality, pinning, unary or additional kernel. S1 alignment applies to the supported canonical network image; arbitrary S1 incidence has no serializer here.
cost: Finite Boolean-stack compiler, original encoded-length polynomial and same-run primitive bound. ExactField answer copying is charged using target outputBound; returned reduction is not LengthControlledOracleReduction. Only an already length-controlled caller is transported by the canonical inlining theorem.
direction: Extension -> base elimination gives base FP -> extension FP and extension hardness -> base hardness. Prefix inclusion gives equivalence. This does not invert D FiniteResources strict RootCode interface without a separately proved representation/cost bridge.
nontrivial_examples: Binary base [[1,2],[3,4]], macro square [[7,10],[15,22]], two occurrences compile to four vertices with fresh edge IDs 2 and 3, value 858. Separate S1 client retains one isolate and two independent internal pairs, six occurrences, value 98. Original 18/32 substitution client remains in All.

title: Fixed-basis exact arithmetic and actual consumers
fixed_parameters: Field K, DecidableEq K where required, Algebra Q K, finite dimension and rational Module.Basis fixed before runtime. Exact numberFieldEncoding basis retained.
runtime_inputs: Field values or actual runtime lists/interpolation tables encoded in that fixed basis.
promises: Field division is total: x/0=0, including 0/0. Coefficient recovery requires its original distinct-node and degree hypotheses. Nonzero divisor is needed only for the client equation equivalence, not for machine execution.
outputs: Original FP actual TM2 certificates, same-computer outputs/time/steps/output-length and intermediate-stack bounds. Arithmetic public aliases resolve to canonical PlanarHom declarations.
resources: No field/basis search, Holant fixed-coordinate/RootCode conversion, or free field operations. Height entry carries dimension/cleared-coordinate budgets separately.
cost: Polynomial in the complete original serialized input. Composition client uses actual pairing/projection and machine composition. Materialized interpolation preserves equality filter, differences, products, divisions, sums and finite-alphabet refinement.
nontrivial_examples: Independent normalize-and-compare computes (7-3)/2=2; zero divisor remains certified. Existing materialized quadratic data returns coefficient two through the new entry.

title: Actual public binary #P downward closure
fixed_parameters: Actual F1 ParsimoniousReduction r and target SharpPWitness w on Computability.encodingList Bool. Source/target counts have codomain Nat.
runtime_inputs: All raw List Bool instances and tagged instance/witness pairs; no extra promise or oracle.
promises: P=q.comp L, where L is derived from the reduction program/time and q is target witness length. Actual predicate rejects too-short witnesses, uses the first t target bits, requires every remaining bit false. No supplied verifier correctness, pair lifting or cost proof is required beyond r and w.
outputs: Explicit source SharpPWitness and InSharpP transport; ParsimoniousReduces.inSharpP and ParsimoniousEquivalent.inSharpP_iff.
resources: Witness preservation is actual machine work through tagged/framed transducers, materialized pair lifting, length/poly evaluation, prefix/suffix scan, target verifier, Boolean conversion and finite alphabet restriction.
cost: The verifier_time_bound is in whole pair encoded length; verifier_steps exposes the actual subrun sum, including retained witness. Pure padded-count equalities remain in Basic; machine construction is separate.
direction: r:f->g and InSharpP(g) imply InSharpP(f), for this standard bits encoding. Arbitrary abstract codecs are not silently generalized.
nontrivial_examples: Reversal-derived L(n)=2n+1 gives five source witness bits for a two-bit target; unique suffix yields count 3, ignored suffix yields 24. True padding, short/empty witness, empty prefix and zero-bit witness are checked; physical pair framing overhead is 32 transitions in the concrete run.

title: Fixed-palette Product S1 input to canonical machine
fixed_parameters: Finite palette values:Fin q->K; machine fixes FixedField K d and rational table Fin q->Fin d->Q. Palette may contain duplicate/zero coefficients.
runtime_inputs: Genuine S1 occurrence list for nullary scalar, unary pair, equality/disequality, explicit unary-coded variable count, finite palette addresses.
promises: Ordered/multiple occurrences, repeated scope variable, nullary factors and isolated variables retained. Input codec is exactly the original LabelledFactor representation transported through proved inverse maps; valid encoded inputs, no extra all-malformed rejection behavior.
outputs: Same S1 partition in F.encoding, actual clean outputs_partition, decode law, identical original machine/time and same-run transition/primitive bounds.
resources: Uses the canonical factor-input Product solver, not RawClosedNetwork/FamilyFieldSolver. It already accepts arbitrary indexed Product factors; no incidence-to-network conversion or extra resource grant to another language is inferred.
cost: No hidden host preprocessing: input bytes are already the original records; conversionComputes is an actual identity-machine witness. variableCount_le_inputLength charges isolates. Original physical parser, elimination, palette lookup, field arithmetic and output cleanup remain in the charged run.
direction: Frontend value/codec transport to existing exact field-valued Holant InFP. No natural-valued #P membership or runtime-variable language/basis algorithm.
nontrivial_examples: Rational palette [0,1,-1,2,3,5]: repeated occurrence/scope + isolate 228; cancellation 0; zero scalar 0; repeated nullaries 18; five isolates 32.
